deviations_from_the_frozen_design: (a) MUTANTS. The freeze named `GateFromConvQuery` (KDA) and `GateFromAttentionOutput` (MLA). Neither closes at the fixtures' deliberately distinct widths — the conv query is `[H·D]`-wide and the attention output `[Hq·v_head_dim]`-wide while `g_proj` reads `hidden`, so the shapes refuse the mutant before any number is produced. Both are recorded UNREACHABLE at this geometry, never as caught. In their place the oracle carries PLACEMENT mutants — `gate_on_value_before_recurrence` (KDA, output rel-L2 0.50, executor arm `GateOnValueBeforeRecurrence`, caught and equal) and `gate_on_values_before_aggregation` (MLA, 0.49) — plus `sigmoid_omitted` on both sides (KDA 1.82, MLA 1.59).

(b) THE MLA PLACEMENT MUTANT HAS NO EXECUTOR ARM. Gating every cached position's value by its OWN gate requires a gate per cached position; the streaming executor caches the compressed latent and decompresses values at read time, so it holds no such state and cannot express the defect. Recorded in `mla_parity_output_gate::the_placement_control_is_measured_by_the_oracle_and_unreachable_here` as an oracle-side fact about the reference's placement claim.

(c) THE HYBRID METAL KDA PATH DOES NOT REFUSE. `kda_metal.rs` offloads q/k/v/o and computes every gate on the CPU path by its own design ('low-rank gates … stay on the proven CPU path'), so a `FullRank` weights value flows through it unchanged and CORRECTLY — the same `project` call the parity arm proved. Refusing there would refuse a proven path; the freeze's 'every Metal path' was written believing the hybrid bound the gate on device. The device-BINDING paths (`kimi_source` -> `stack_metal` -> `KdaDeviceWeights`, and the MLA device path) are the ones that would silently mis-bind, and those refuse through `declared_gate_refusal`.
(d) P4's spelling count: 13 forecast, 12 measured (per-layer spellings). The forecast mis-read the estate list's granularity; the tensor counts were right.
(e) P10's quartet moved to the op-plan witness (see P10).
(f) The baseline arm was origin/main after #435 merged (8a0067a3) rather than #435's head; identical semantics (18) and, measured, identical numbers.

(g) The synthetic closure fixture's `g_proj` is square (`[32, 32]`: hidden 32 = 4 heads x 8) on both operators, so its shape contract cannot separate a transposed gate; the parity arms carry the distinct widths (`[8, 6]` and `[10, 7]`), and the closure witness is about declaration/estate agreement, not arithmetic.
findings: The plan's own operand view (`planned_operands()`) did not list the new gate matrices, and the FIRST end-to-end execution of a full-rank estate was refused by the existing loader/plan agreement check: 'the loader resolves an operand the plan's own view does not list'. The check did its job; the view now lists both gate matrices.

The production encoder refuses to KEEP an estate whose operands do not close, naming the tensor and what it implies (e.g. `0.self_attn.g_proj.weight` … 'declares no `use_full_rank_gate`'). The closure witness therefore encodes through the graph seam (as `k3_attnres_addressing` does) and carries one production-encoder arm proving both refusals and both acceptances.
